title: Bekhorot 28
description: How long a blemished firstborn may be kept beyond its first year, and the refutation of Rabbi Elazar; Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda on a firstborn slaughtered before its blemish was shown to an expert; and what a non-expert, a judge or an expert pays when he rules wrongly, with the story of Rabbi Tarfon’s cow.
topics: 🍖 “It shall be yours”: a second day for eating the firstborn, or a blemished firstborn for the priest?
📅 Twelve months and thirty days: how long a blemished firstborn may be kept
❌ Rabbi Elazar’s “thirty days after its year” is refuted
👁️ Slaughtered first, examined after: blemishes in the eye change after death, those on the body do not
💰 The non-expert examiner pays a quarter for a sheep and half for a bull
⚖️ A judge who errs: what he did is done and he pays, unless he is an expert for the court
🐄 Rabbi Tarfon’s cow, Todos the doctor and “Your donkey is gone, Tarfon”

a1.he: וְאִידַּךְ, אִי מֵהָתָם אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר חָזֶה וָשׁוֹק שֶׁל תּוֹדָה.

a2.he: וְאִידַּךְ, אָמַר קְרָא: ״לְךָ יִהְיֶה״ — הוֹסִיף לְךָ הַכָּתוּב הֲוָיָה אַחֶרֶת בִּבְכוֹר.

a3.he: וְאִידַּךְ, הָא מֵהָתָם אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר: הַאי ״יִהְיֶה לָּךְ״ — לִימֵּד עַל בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁנּוֹתְנוֹ לְכֹהֵן, שֶׁלֹּא מָצִינוּ לוֹ בְּכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ.

a4.he: וְאִידַּךְ, אָמַר ״וּבְשָׂרָם״ — אֶחָד תָּם וְאֶחָד בַּעַל מוּם, וְאִידַּךְ — ״וּבְשָׂרָם״ דְּהָנֵי בְּכוֹרוֹת דְּכוּלְּהוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָאָמַר.

a5.he: נוֹלַד לוֹ מוּם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ, רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הֵיכִי קָאָמַר? נוֹלַד לוֹ בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ, רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ, וּלְאַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ נָמֵי שְׁלֹשִׁים? אוֹ דִלְמָא: הֵיכָא דְּנוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ, רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ וְתוּ לָא, וְהֵיכָא דְּנוֹלַד לוֹ אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ, אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ אֶלָּא שְׁלֹשִׁים?

a6.he: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא: בְּכוֹר בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה, עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאָה לְהַרְאוֹתוֹ לֶחָכָם — רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ שְׁתַּיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים, וּמִשֶּׁנִּרְאָה לְהַרְאוֹתוֹ לֶחָכָם, נוֹלַד לוֹ מוּם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ — רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.

a7.he: אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ אֲפִילּוּ יוֹם אֶחָד, וַאֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת. אֲבָל מִפְּנֵי הֲשָׁבַת אֲבֵידָה לַבְּעָלִים, אָמְרוּ: רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.

a8.he: וַעֲדַיִין תִּיבְּעֵי לִי: שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ, אוֹ דִלְמָא קוֹדֶם שְׁנָתוֹ?

a9.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: נוֹלַד לוֹ מוּם בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ, מַשְׁלִימִין לוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, מְסַיַּיע לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: נוֹתְנִין לוֹ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם.

a10.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִנַּיִן לִבְכוֹר שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין לוֹ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה״, (אֵיזוֹ) [אֵילּוּ] הֵן יָמִים הַחֲשׁוּבִין שָׁנָה — הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.

a11.he: מֵיתִיבִי: נוֹלַד לוֹ מוּם בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ — מַשְׁלִימִין לוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ. הַשְׁלָמָה — אִין, מֵיהֲבָא — לָא! תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, תְּיוּבְתָּא.

a12.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַבְּכוֹר וּמַרְאֶה אֶת מוּמוֹ — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: הוֹאִיל וְנִשְׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי מוּמְחֶה — אָסוּר. מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּמְחֶה וְרוֹאֶה אֶת הַבְּכוֹר, וְנִשְׁחַט עַל פִּיו — הֲרֵי זֶה יִקָּבֵר, וִישַׁלֵּם מִבֵּיתוֹ.

a13.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: בְּדוּקִּין שֶׁבָּעַיִן — דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּאָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מִשְׁתַּנִּין. לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּמוּמִין שֶׁבַּגּוּף, דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: גָּזְרִינַן מוּמִין שֶׁבַּגּוּף אַטּוּ דּוּקִּין שֶׁבָּעַיִן, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: לָא גָּזְרִינַן מוּמִין שֶׁבַּגּוּף אַטּוּ דּוּקִּין שֶׁבָּעַיִן.

a14.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַבְּכוֹר וּמַרְאֶה אֶת מוּמָיו — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּדוּקִּין שֶׁבְּעַיִן אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מִשְׁתַּנִּין, בְּמוּמִין שֶׁבַּגּוּף מוּתָּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין מִשְׁתַּנִּין. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מִשְׁתַּנִּין. מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מִשְׁתַּנִּין סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ? מוּמִין שֶׁבַּגּוּף מִי מִשְׁתַּנִּין?! אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי הַמִּשְׁתַּנִּין.

b1.he: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: הוֹאִיל וְנִשְׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי מוּמְחֶה אָסוּר. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קְנָסָא קָא קָנֵיס רַבִּי מֵאִיר, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

b2.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִפְּנֵי הַמִּשְׁתַּנִּין — דְּכוּלְּהוּ מִשְׁתַּנִּי, אוֹ דִלְמָא אִיכָּא דְּמִשְׁתַּנֵּי וְאִיכָּא דְּלָא מִשְׁתַּנֵּי?

b3.he: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? לְאַכְחוֹשֵׁי סָהֲדִי. אִי אָמְרַתְּ: כּוּלְּהוּ מִשְׁתַּנִּי — שַׁקָּרֵי נִינְהוּ, וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ: אִיכָּא דְּמִשְׁתַּנֵּי וְאִיכָּא דְּלָא מִשְׁתַּנֵּי — סָמְכִינַן עֲלַיְיהוּ. מַאי?

b4.he: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: שָׂח לִי רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה דְּמִן אוּשָׁא, בֹּא וְאַרְאֶךָּ בְּדוּקִּין שֶׁהֵן מִשְׁתַּנִּים. מִדְּקָאָמַר לֵיהּ ״בֹּא וְאַרְאֶךָּ״, מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא דְּמִשְׁתַּנֵּי וְאִיכָּא דְּלָא מִשְׁתַּנֵּי.

b5.he: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּמְחֶה, וְרָאָה אֶת הַבְּכוֹר וְנִשְׁחַט עַל פִּיו, הֲרֵי זֶה יִקָּבֵר, וִישַׁלֵּם מִבֵּיתוֹ. לֵימָא תְּנַן סְתָמָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר? דִּלְמָא בְּדוּקִּין שֶׁבָּעַיִן, וְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל.

b6.he: תָּנָא: כְּשֶׁהוּא מְשַׁלֵּם — מְשַׁלֵּם רְבִיעַ לַדַּקָּה, וּמֶחֱצָה לַגַּסָּה. מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: זֶה הֶפְסֵד מְרוּבֶּה, וְזֶה הֶפְסֵד מוּעָט.

b7.he: אִי הָכִי, לְפוּם פְּסֵידָא לִישַׁלֵּם! אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר אִיקָא: מִשּׁוּם גְּזֵירַת מְגַדְּלֵי בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה נָגְעוּ בָּהּ.

b8.he: מַתְנִי׳ דָּן אֶת הַדִּין, זִיכָּה אֶת הַחַיָּיב וְחִיֵּיב אֶת הַזַּכַּאי, טִימֵּא אֶת הַטָּהוֹר וְטִיהֵר אֶת הַטָּמֵא — מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה עָשׂוּי, וִישַׁלֵּם מִבֵּיתוֹ. וְאִם הָיָה מוּמְחֶה לְבֵית דִּין — פָּטוּר מִלְּשַׁלֵּם.

b9.he: גְּמָ׳ לֵימָא תְּנַן סְתָמָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּדָאֵין דִּינָא דִּגְרָמֵי? אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא אָמַר רַב: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּשָׂא וְנָתַן בַּיָּד.

b10.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא חִיֵּיב אֶת הַזַּכַּאי — כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּשָׂא וְנָתַן בַּיָּד, אֶלָּא זִיכָּה אֶת הַחַיָּיב הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִי דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ ״פָּטוּר אַתָּה״ — וְהָא לֹא נָשָׂא וְנָתַן בַּיָּד! אָמַר רָבִינָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ מַשְׁכּוֹן וּנְטָלוֹ הֵימֶנּוּ.

b11.he: טִימֵּא אֶת הַטָּהוֹר — דְּאַגַּע בְּהוּ שֶׁרֶץ, טִיהֵר אֶת הַטָּמֵא — שֶׁעֵירְבָן עִם פֵּירוֹתָיו.

b12.he: מַתְנִי׳ וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּפָרָה שֶׁנִּיטְּלָה הָאֵם שֶׁלָּהּ, וְהֶאֱכִילָהּ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן לִכְלָבִים, וּבָא מַעֲשֶׂה לִפְנֵי חֲכָמִים בְּיַבְנֶה, וְהִתִּירוּהָ.

b13.he: וְאָמַר תּוֹדוֹס הָרוֹפֵא: אֵין פָּרָה וַחֲזִירָה יוֹצְאָה מֵאֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִיָּא שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁאֵין חוֹתְכִין הָאֵם שֶׁלָּהּ, בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא תֵּלֵד.

b14.he: אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן: הָלְכָה חֲמוֹרְךָ טַרְפוֹן! אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן, אַתָּה מוּמְחֶה לְבֵית דִּין, וְכׇל הַמּוּמְחֶה לְבֵית דִּין פָּטוּר מִלְּשַׁלֵּם.

b15.he: גְּמָ׳ וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ, דְּטָעָה בִּדְבַר מִשְׁנָה, וְטָעָה בִּדְבַר מִשְׁנָה חוֹזֵר!

b16.he: חֲדָא וְעוֹד קָאָמַר: חֲדָא — דְּטָעָה בִּדְבַר מִשְׁנָה חוֹזֵר, וְעוֹד — אִי נָמֵי בְּשִׁיקּוּל הַדַּעַת טָעִיתָה, מוּמְחֶה לְבֵית דִּין אַתָּה, וְכׇל הַמּוּמְחֶה לְבֵית דִּין פָּטוּר מִלְּשַׁלֵּם.

b17.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַנּוֹטֵל שָׂכָר לִהְיוֹת רוֹאֶה אֶת הַבְּכוֹרוֹת — אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין עַל פִּיו, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה מוּמְחֶה.

messages.text: Continued from 27b: Rav derives that a firstborn is eaten for two days and one night from “And their flesh shall be yours, as the breast of waving and as the right thigh,” while the school of Rav derives it from “year by year.”
And the other ones, i.e., the Sages from the school of Rav, why don’t they derive the halakha that a firstborn is eaten for two days and one night from that verse?

notes.he: דמפיק מובשרם יהיה לך וגו' ההוא ודאי בחזה ושוק דתודה מישתעי אלא שני ימים נפקא ליה מיהיה לך דמשמע הויה אחרת לבר מזו:
notes.en: And the other [Rav], who derives it from “And their flesh shall be yours…”: that [comparison by itself] certainly speaks of the breast and thigh of a thanks offering. Rather, he derives the two days from “it shall be yours,” which implies another “being” beyond this one.

messages.text: If it were derived from there, it would be possible to say that the verse is comparing the halakha of a firstborn to the breast and thigh of a thanks offering, which are eaten for only one day and night.

notes.dh: הוה אמינא בחזה ושוק של תודה
notes.he: לר' עקיבא לית ליה כי הך סברא בסוף איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נז.) ומפרש דהתם פליגי בהימנו ודבר אחר אי הוי היקש או לא:
notes.en: One might say: the breast and thigh of a thanks offering: Rabbi Akiva does not accept this reasoning, at the end of Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 57a); and it explains there that they disagree about “from it” and something else, whether it counts as a juxtaposition [hekesh] or not.

notes.dh: איכא למימר בחזה ושוק של תודה
notes.he: והיינו נמי שלמים ואינו נאכל אלא ליום ולילה:
notes.en: One could say: the breast and thigh of a thanks offering, which is also [a kind of] peace offering, yet is eaten only for a day and a night.

messages.text: And the other one, Rav Yehuda, citing Rav, how does he respond to this?

The verse states: “And their flesh shall be yours, as the breast of waving and as the right thigh, it shall be yours” (Numbers 18:18). The verse adds another mention of a form of the term being in the second phrase: “It shall be yours,” to teach that the priest has an additional day to eat a firstborn animal, i.e., that it is compared to the breast and thigh of a peace offering, not to that of a thanks offering.

verse.he: וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה־לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וּכְשׁוֹק הַיָּמִין לְךָ יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: But their meat shall be yours: it shall be yours like the breast of elevation offering and like the right thigh.

messages.text: And the other ones, the Sages from the school of Rav, how do they respond to this claim?

With regard to the inference from there, it is possible to say that this phrase: “It shall be yours,” teaches with regard to a blemished firstborn that the owner must give it to the priest. This derivation is necessary, as we have not found this halakha that a blemished firstborn is given to a priest stated explicitly anywhere in the entire Torah.

notes.he: שיתננו לכהן אלא מרבויא דהאי יהיה לך נפקא:
notes.en: For we have not found in the entire Torah: that he gives it to the priest, except from the amplification of this “it shall be yours.”

notes.dh: שלא מצינו לו בכל התורה כולה
notes.he: פי' בקונטרס שיתננו לכהן אלא מריבויא לפירושו כן יכול לומר בכל דרשות ומפרש ר"י דהכי קאמר שלא מצינו לו בכל התורה כולה שיתננו כולה כיוצא בזה דחטאת ואשם שהם לכהן כשקריבין למזבח אם הוממו שהמזבח מפסיד חלקו מפסיד גם לכהן אבל בכור אפילו בעל מום דכהן הוא וכן ההיא דפרק שתי מדות (מנחות דף צא:) גבי נסכים לכבש האחד זה אחד עשר של מעשר שלא מצינו לו בכל התורה כולה שיהא טפל חמור מן העיקר דהוה מצי למימר אחד עשר של מעשר יוכיח כדמשני אמותר מפסח וכן בשבת בפ' אמר ר' עקיבא (שבת דף פג:) זה היסטו של זב שלא מצינו בכל התורה כולה דטומאה המסטת תטמא:
notes.en: For we have not found for it in the entire Torah: Rashi explained: that he gives it to the priest, except from the amplification. [But] by his explanation one could say this of every exposition. The Ri explains that this is what it means: we have not found anything like it in the entire Torah, that he gives it entirely [to the priest]. For a sin offering and a guilt offering, which belong to the priest when they are offered on the altar, if they became blemished, then since the altar loses its share, the priest loses too; but a firstborn, even a blemished one, belongs to the priest. And similarly that passage in chapter Shtei Middot (Menachot 91b) about libations, “for the one lamb”: this is the eleventh [animal] of the tithe, “for we have not found in the entire Torah that the secondary is more stringent than the primary,” though one could have said: let the eleventh of the tithe prove [otherwise], as it answers there concerning the leftover of a Passover offering. And similarly in Shabbat, chapter Amar Rabbi Akiva (Shabbat 83b): this is the moving of a zav, “for we have not found in the entire Torah that impurity by moving imparts impurity.”

notes.he: שלא מצינו בכל התורה דבכור בעל מום לכהן אלא מהכא:
notes.en: For we have not found in the entire Torah that a blemished firstborn [goes] to the priest, except from here.

messages.text: And the other one, Rav Yehuda, citing Rav, from where does he derive that a blemished firstborn is given to a priest?
The verse states: “And their flesh shall be yours,” in the plural, i.e., both an unblemished firstborn and a blemished firstborn.

notes.he: דמפיק מיהיה לך שני ימים ולילה אחת בכור בעל מום שניתן לכהן מובשרם יהיה לך נפקא לשון רבים משמע אחד תם ואחד בעל מום:
notes.en: And the other [Rav], who derives two days and one night from “it shall be yours”: that a blemished firstborn is given to the priest he derives from “and their flesh,” which is plural: both an unblemished one and a blemished one.

messages.text: And the other ones, the Sages from the school of Rav, how do they respond? They would claim that the term “and their flesh” is written in the plural not because it is referring to blemished animals, but because it is said in reference to those firstborn animals of all the Israelites.

notes.he: לא משמע אלא תמימים והא דנקט לשון רבים דאבכורות דכולהו ישראל קאי:
notes.en: And the other: “and their flesh” implies only unblemished ones, and it uses the plural because it refers to the firstborn of all Israel.

notes.dh: ואידך ובשרם דהני בכורות דכולהו ישראל קאמר
notes.he: בסוף איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נז.) משני רבי ישמעאל מבשרם דהנך [בכורות] קאמר משמע רוצה לומר דקאי אבכור שור וכשב ועז דכתיב לעיל מיניה ושינויא אחרינא הוא וא"ת והא תנא לא דריש מידי מובשרם לשון רבים ובסוגיא דהתם לעיל (שם דף נו:) דריש ר' יוסי הגלילי דמו לא נאמר אלא דמם חלבו לא נאמר אלא חלבם לימד על בכור ומעשר שטעונין מתן דמים ואמורין למזבח וי"ל דפלוגתא היא בר"פ בית שמאי בזבחים (דף לז.) ורבי ישמעאל נפקא ליה מדם זבחיך ישפך:
notes.en: And the other: “and their flesh” speaks of the firstborn of all Israel: At the end of Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 57a), Rabbi Yishmael answers: “and their flesh” speaks of these [firstborn], which means it refers to the firstborn of the ox, the sheep and the goat written just before it; that is a different answer. And if you ask: but the tanna expounds nothing from the plural “and their flesh,” yet in the discussion there earlier (Zevachim 56b) Rabbi Yosei HaGelili expounds: it does not say “its blood” but “their blood,” not “its fat” but “their fat,” teaching about the firstborn and the tithe that they require placement of the blood and of the sacrificial portions on the altar? One can say that this is a dispute, at the beginning of chapter Beit Shammai in Zevachim (37a), and Rabbi Yishmael derives it from “and the blood of your offerings shall be poured out.”

notes.he: דהני בכורות קאמר אך בכור כשב או בכור עז וגו' מתמימים ולא מבעלי מומין:
notes.en: “And their flesh”: it speaks of these firstborn [“But the firstborn of an ox, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat…”], of unblemished ones and not of blemished ones. [An editor’s note: Rabbeinu Gershom’s reading here matches Zevachim 57a; see Tosafot here.]

messages.text: If a blemish developed within its first year, it is permitted for the owner to maintain the animal for the entire twelve months; if a blemish developed after twelve months have passed, it is permitted for the owner to maintain the animal for only thirty days.
A dilemma was raised before the Sages: With regard to what case is the mishna speaking?
messages.quote: permitted for the owner to maintain the animal for the entire twelve months

messages.text: Does the mishna mean that if a blemish developed within the animal’s first year, the owner is permitted to maintain the animal for the entire twelve months, and after the animal’s first year also for another thirty days?

notes.he: אף על גב דמום בתוך שנתו נולד טובא:
notes.en: And after its year also thirty days: even though the blemish developed within its year, long before.

notes.he: עד שיהו לו שנים עשר חדש משנולד:
notes.en: All twelve months: until it is twelve months old from its birth.

messages.text: Or perhaps the mishna is referring to two different situations, i.e., in a case where the blemish developed within the animal’s first year the owner is permitted to maintain the animal for the entire twelve months, but nothing more; and in a case where it developed a blemish after one year, he is permitted to maintain it for only thirty days.

notes.dh: היכא דנולד בו מום לאחר שנתו
notes.he: רשאי לקיימו שלשים יום משנולד המום דלאחר שנתו דמתני' ה"ק ואם לאחר שנתו נולד המום יקיימנו שלשים יום:
notes.en: Where a blemish developed after its year: he may keep it thirty days from when the blemish developed after its year. And this is what the mishna means: and if the blemish developed after its year, he keeps it thirty days.

messages.text: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:

With regard to a firstborn in the present time, when there is no Temple and the animal cannot be brought as an offering, until it has developed a blemish that can be shown to an expert, it is permitted for the owner to maintain the animal for two or three years. But once the animal develops a blemish that can be shown to an expert, if the blemish developed within its first year, it is permitted for the owner to maintain it for the entire twelve months.

notes.he: שאין תם ראוי לכלום:
notes.en: In the present time: when an unblemished [firstborn] is fit for nothing.

notes.he: שלא נפל בו מום אחר שנתו:
notes.en: Before it is fit to be shown to an expert: that no blemish has befallen it, [even] after its year.

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס שלא נפל בו מום וקשה מאי רשאי לקיימו שתים ושלש שנים על כרחיך יקיימנו ודוחק לפרש רשאי לשון חייב כי ההיא דערכין (דף כח:) דמקדישין אותו הקדש עילוי כמה אדם רוצה ליתן בקרבן זה לעשותו עולה אע"פ שאינו רשאי דפירושו כמו אע"פ שאינו חייב והוה מצינן לפרש דנקט רשאי לקיימו כלומר ואין זקוק לכונסו לכיפה אע"ג דשאר קדשים שהקדיש והחרים בזמן הזה אמרינן בפ"ק דע"ז (דף יג.) בהמה תעקר דנועל דלת בפניה והיא מתה מאיליה אבל היה משמע דאם היה רוצה לכונסו לכיפה כונסו ומעשים בכל יום ששומרים אותם עד שיפול בהם מום ונראה לפרש עד שלא נראה להראותו לחכם שלא נזדמן לו חכם אחר שנפל בו מום שאין זקוק להוליכו במקום רחוק למקום שהחכם שם:
notes.en: Before it is fit to be shown to an expert: Rashi explained: that no blemish has befallen it. This is difficult: what does “he is permitted to keep it two or three years” mean? He must keep it regardless! And it is forced to explain “permitted” as “obligated,” like that passage in Arakhin (28b): one consecrates it with a consecration of its value, as much as a person would want to give for this offering to make it a burnt offering, even though he is not permitted, which means “even though he is not obligated.” We could explain that it says “permitted to keep it” meaning: and he need not confine it in a cell [to die], even though for other sacred animals that one consecrated or devoted in the present time we say in the first chapter of Avoda Zara (13a): the animal is hamstrung, [or] one locks the door before it and it dies of itself. But that would imply that if he wanted to confine it in a cell he could, and it is an everyday practice that people keep them until a blemish befalls them. It seems [better] to explain “before it is fit to be shown to an expert”: that no expert happened to be available after the blemish befell it, [and] he need not take it far away to the place where the expert is.

notes.he: כלומר קודם שיפול בו מום רשאי לקיימו ב' או ג' שנים אם אין שם כהן:
notes.en: Before it is fit to be shown to an expert: that is, before a blemish befalls it, he may keep it two or three years if there is no priest there.

messages.text: After the animal’s first year, the owner does not have permission to maintain it even for one day, or even one hour. But due to the mitzva of returning a lost item to the owners, i.e., to give the owner time to find a priest and give him the animal, the Sages said: The owner is permitted to maintain the animal for thirty days.

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס דהיינו כהן דזימנין דלא משכח כהן למיתבא ליה ואם ישחטנו מיד יסרח לפיכך רשאי לקיימו שלשים יום אחר שנתו ואומר רבי דמיירי ביד כהן וא"צ עכשיו לבשר ונתנו לו חכמים זמן ל' יום אבל ישראל לעולם ממתין עד שימצא כהן:
notes.en: Due to returning a lost item to the owners: Rashi explained: that is, the priest, for sometimes he will not find a priest to give it to, and if he slaughters it at once it will rot; therefore he may keep it thirty days after its year. And Rabbi [Tosafot’s teacher] says that it speaks of [a firstborn] in the priest’s hands who does not need meat now, and the Sages gave him a period of thirty days; but an Israelite always waits until he finds a priest.

notes.he: כלומר כשנפל בו מום אבל מפני השב אבדה לבעלים אמרו רשאי לקיימו ל' יום דבין כך ובין כך שמא יבא כהן שאם ישחטנו קודם שמא יסריח קודם שיבא כהן:
notes.en: And once it is fit to be shown: that is, when a blemish befell it. But due to returning a lost item to the owners they said he may keep it thirty days, for in the meantime perhaps a priest will come; for if he slaughters it earlier, perhaps it will rot before a priest comes.

messages.text: In its latter clause, the baraita is presumably still addressing a blemish that developed in the first year. If so, the thirty days evidently apply in such a case.

notes.dh: אינו רשאי לקיימו אפילו יום אחד
notes.he: וקס"ד אנולד בו מום בתוך שנתו קאי וקתני אבל מפני השבת אבידה לבעלים דהיינו כהן דשמא אם ביד ישראל הוי האי בכור לא משכח כהן למיתבי ליה ואי שחיט ליה יסריח הבשר אמרו רשאי לקיימו ל' יום ואי לא משכח כהן שוחטו ומולחו עד שימצא כהן. אלמא ל' יום דקאמר אנולד מום בתוך שנתו קאי:
notes.en: He is not permitted to keep it even one day: it is presently assumed that this refers to a blemish that developed within its year, and it teaches: but due to returning a lost item to the owners, that is, the priest. For perhaps, while this firstborn is in the Israelite’s hands, he will not find a priest to give it to, and if he slaughters it the meat will rot; [so] they said he may keep it thirty days, and if he does not find a priest he slaughters it and salts it until he finds a priest. Evidently the thirty days it mentions refer to a blemish that developed within its year.

messages.text: But still, let the dilemma be raised with regard to that baraita itself: Are the thirty days granted in a case where the animal develops a blemish after its first year? Or perhaps these thirty days are granted if it develops a blemish before the end of its first year. In other words, when the baraita states: After its first year, this can be interpreted as referring to an animal whose blemish developed only then, or to one that had a blemish earlier and subsequently reached the end of its first year.

notes.he: דברייתא גופה איכא לספוקא דאיכא למימר הא דקתני לאחר שנתו אין רשאי לקיימו כו' הכי קאמר נולד בו לאחר שנתו אין רשאי לקיימו כו' ועלה קאי אבל מפני השבת אבידה כו':
notes.en: Still let it be asked: in the baraita itself there is room for doubt. One can say that what it teaches, “after its year he is not permitted to keep it…,” means: if [the blemish] developed after its year he is not permitted to keep it etc., and it is on this that “but due to returning a lost item…” stands.

notes.he: כלומר אם נולד מום קודם שנתו נמי קאמר דלאחר שנתו שלשים יום:
notes.en: Or perhaps before its year: that is, if the blemish developed before its year, it also says that after its year [he has] thirty days.

notes.he: הנולד לו מום בתוך שנתו או לאחר שנתו דודאי היכא דנולד לו לאחר שנתו יכול לקיימו עוד ל' אבל אם נולד לו מום קודם אם יוכל לקיימו כל שנתו ושוב ל' משלימין לו חמשה עשר יום אחר שנתו אלמא דנותנין לו ל' אחר מומו ולא ל' אחר שנתו כשנפל בו מום בתוך שנתו:
notes.en: And still let the question be asked about the thirty days: [do they apply to one] that developed a blemish within its year or after its year? For certainly where it developed after its year he may keep it another thirty; but if it developed a blemish earlier, [the question is] whether he may keep it all its year and then thirty more. “One completes for it fifteen days after its year”: evidently one gives him thirty after its blemish, and not thirty after its year, when a blemish befell it within its year.

messages.text: Come and hear a baraita:
If the animal developed a blemish on the fifteenth day within its first year, i.e., fifteen days before the end of its year, one completes for it fifteen days after its year.
Conclude from this baraita that the owner may maintain a firstborn for an additional thirty days if it develops the blemish during its first year.

notes.he: אלמא ל' יום דקתני מתני' אנולד בו מום לאחר שנתו קאי דאי נולד המום בתוך שנתו אפילו יום אחד ליכא למימר דניתב ליה אחר שנתו שלשים יום דלית ליה אלא השלמה כדקתני בברייתא ושמעינן מינה דאי בתוך שנתו נולד המום חדש או חדשים רשאי לקיימו עד שנתו דהא כתיב שנה ואי לאחר שנה נולד מום או קרוב לסיום שנתו יהבינן ליה שלשים יום משנולד המום:
notes.en: One completes for it fifteen days after its year: evidently the thirty days the mishna teaches refer to a blemish that developed after its year. For if the blemish developed within its year, even only one day [before its end], one cannot say that we give him thirty days after its year, since he has only the completion, as the baraita teaches. And we learn from it that if the blemish developed within its year, a month or two [before its end], he may keep it until [the end of] its year, since “year” is written; and if the blemish developed after the year, or close to the end of its year, we give him thirty days from when the blemish developed.

notes.dh: אבל אם נולד בו מום לאחר שנתו נותנין לו ל' אחר שנתו
notes.he: ואם נולד בו מום בתחלת שנתו נותנין לו כל שנתו ולא יותר:
notes.en: But if a blemish developed after its year, one gives him thirty after its year; and if a blemish developed at the beginning of its year, one gives him all its year and no more.

messages.text: This supports the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, as Rabbi Elazar says:
With regard to an animal that developed a blemish toward the end of its year, one gives the owner thirty days from the time that the animal developed a blemish.

notes.he: אם נולד מום אחר שנתו:
notes.en: One gives him thirty days: if the blemish developed after its year.

notes.he: אם נולד בו מום בסוף שנתו:
notes.en: From the time a blemish developed: if a blemish developed at the end of its year.

messages.text: From where is it derived with regard to a firstborn animal that developed a blemish during its first year that one gives the owner thirty days after its year? It is derived from a verse, as it is stated: “You shall eat it before the Lord your God year by year in the place that the Lord shall choose, you and your household” (Deuteronomy 15:20). It is derived from here that it may be eaten for one year and for another year. Which are the days that are considered to be a significant part of a year? You must say these are thirty days, which in certain respects are considered a complete year. This indicates that such a firstborn may be eaten for up to thirty days beyond the first twelve months.
messages.lead: There are those who say that Rabbi Elazar says:

verse.he: לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אַתָּה וּבֵיתֶךָ׃
verse.en: You and your household shall eat it annually before the ETERNAL your God in the place that GOD will choose.

notes.he: שתי שנים משמע. שלשים יום בשנה חשובין שנה לדברי הכל בפירקא קמא דראש השנה (דף י:):
notes.en: Year by year: implies two years. Thirty days in a year count as a year, according to all, in the first chapter of Rosh HaShana (10b).

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita that if the animal developed a blemish on the fifteenth day within its year, i.e., fifteen days before the end of its year, one completes for it fifteen days after its year.
messages.lead: According to this version of the discussion, the Gemara raises an objection:
messages.quote: one gives the owner thirty days after its year

messages.text: This indicates that with regard to completing a total of thirty days from the time the animal developed the blemish, yes, the owner may continue to maintain the animal in such a case. But if the blemish developed earlier, the baraita does not give him an extra thirty days beyond the conclusion of the year.

notes.he: מיהבא שלשים יום שלימים לא יהבינן:
notes.en: Completion, yes; giving, no: giving him thirty full days, we do not.

notes.he: כלומר דלא יהבינן ליה לאחר שנתו כלום:
notes.en: Completion, yes; giving, no: that is, we do not give him anything after its year [beyond the completion].

messages.text: ✖ The refutation of the opinion of Rabbi Elazar is indeed a conclusive refutation.

messages.caption: How long the owner may keep a blemished firstborn, by when the blemish appeared.

messages.text: Mishna

In the case of one who slaughters the firstborn animal and only then shows its blemish to an expert to determine whether it is a blemish, and it was established by the expert that it is in fact a blemish that renders its slaughter permitted:

notes.he: לאחר שחיטה ונמצא קבוע:
notes.en: Mishna. And shows its blemish: after the slaughter, and it is found to be permanent.

notes.dh: השוחט את הבכור ומראה את מומו
notes.he: (למימרא) [כלומר] לאחר ששחטו:
notes.en: One who slaughters the firstborn and shows its blemish: that is, after he slaughtered it.

messages.text: for a priest to derive benefit from the firstborn.

notes.he: הואיל ומראו לחכם:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda permits: since he showed it to an expert.

messages.text: Since it was slaughtered not according to the ruling of an expert, it is prohibited.

notes.dh: ר' מאיר אומר הואיל ונשחט שלא על פי מומחה
notes.he: כלומר הואיל ולא הראהו קודם שחיטה אע"פ שמראה לו לאחר שחיטה והוי מום קבוע אפילו הכי קניס רבי מאיר דאסור:
notes.en: Rabbi Meir says: since it was slaughtered not according to an expert: that is, since he did not show it before the slaughter. Even though he shows it to him after the slaughter and it is a permanent blemish, even so Rabbi Meir penalizes [him], and it is forbidden.

messages.text: In a case involving one who is not an expert, and he examined the firstborn animal and it was slaughtered on the basis of his ruling, that animal must be buried, and the non-expert must pay compensation to the priest from his property.
Gemara

The dispute in the mishna between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda does not apply in the case of a blemish on the cornea of the eye. In that situation everyone agrees that the animal is prohibited, because such blemishes in the eye change after the animal’s death, which means that there is no way of determining at that late stage whether it had been a permanent blemish or a temporary one.
messages.quote: one who slaughters the firstborn animal and only then shows its blemish

notes.he: טייל"א כמו הנוטה כדוק שמים (ישעיהו מ):
notes.en: Gemara. Dukin [the cornea]: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss), as in “who stretches out the heavens like a thin film [dok]” (Isaiah 40:22).

notes.he: אם מראה אותם לאחר שחיטה דברי הכל אסור. מפני שהן משתנין לאחר מיתה:
notes.en: With dukin of the eye: if he shows them after the slaughter, all agree it is forbidden, because they change after death.

messages.text: They disagree only with regard to blemishes that are on the animal’s body, which do not change after death. As Rabbi Meir holds that we issue a decree prohibiting the animal in the case of blemishes that are on the animal’s body due to the case of blemishes on the cornea, and Rabbi Yehuda holds that we do not issue a decree with regard to blemishes that are on the animal’s body due to the case of blemishes on the cornea.

notes.dh: רבי מאיר סבר גזרינן מומין שבגוף כו'
notes.he: ואומר רבי דאע"ג דאמרינן בריש אף על פי (כתובות דף נז.) דהלכה כרבי מאיר בגזירותיו הך דהכא קרי ליה בסמוך קנסא דקא קניס ר' מאיר ובשאלתות דרב אחאי פירש דהלכה כמותו דוקא בגזירותיו ולא בקנסא ופסקו דאין הלכה כמותו בההיא דמעוברת חברו ומינקת חברו דקאמר רבי מאיר יוציא ולא יחזיר עולמית וסוגיא דשמעתין בריש החולץ (יבמות דף לז.) דלא כר' מאיר וכן סוגיא דשמעתין כרבי יהודה דלרבי מאיר קנסינן בכולהו מפני המשתנין ובסמוך דקאמר לימא תנן סתמא כרבי מאיר הא משני דילמא בדוקין שבעין ודברי הכל וכן הוא אמת ומתוך כך פוסק רבי דלא כרבי מאיר דקניס בשטר שיש בו רבית דאין גובה לא את הקרן ולא את הרבית (ב"מ דף עב.):
notes.en: Rabbi Meir holds that we decree [for] blemishes on the body…: And Rabbi [Tosafot’s teacher] says: even though we say at the beginning of Af Al Pi (Ketubot 57a) that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir in his decrees, this one here is called just below a penalty that Rabbi Meir imposes; and the She’iltot of Rav Aḥai explains that the halakha follows him only in his decrees and not in [his] penalties. And they ruled that the halakha does not follow him in the case of another man’s pregnant or nursing wife, where Rabbi Meir says he must divorce her and never take her back; and the discussion at the beginning of HaḤoletz (Yevamot 37a) does not follow Rabbi Meir. Likewise the discussion here follows Rabbi Yehuda, for according to Rabbi Meir we would penalize in every case on account of those that change; and below, where it asks, “Shall we say we learned the unattributed mishna in accordance with Rabbi Meir?” it answers: perhaps with dukin of the eye, and it is the opinion of all. And so it is in truth. On this basis Rabbi rules not in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who penalizes [the lender] in a document that contains interest, that he collects neither the principal nor the interest (Bava Metzia 72a).

messages.text: This is also taught in a baraita:
In the case of one who slaughters a firstborn animal and afterward shows its blemishes to an expert:

If the blemish is on the cornea of the eye the animal is prohibited, because such blemishes change. But in the case of blemishes on its body the animal is permitted, because these blemishes do not change.

notes.he: מפני צער מיתה משתנה העין ואף על גב דהשתא מיתחזי קבוע אי הוה חזי ליה מחיים הוה מיתחזי עובר:
notes.en: They change: because of the pain of death the eye changes; and even though now it looks permanent, had he seen it while it was alive it would have looked passing.

notes.he: כגון נסדקה אזנו:
notes.en: On the body: for example, its ear was split.

messages.text: Both this, blemishes on the eye, and that, blemishes on the body, are prohibited because they change.
Could it enter your mind that blemishes on the body are prohibited because they change? Do blemishes on the body change after the death of the animal?
Rather, the blemishes on the body are prohibited due to a decree based on the case of blemishes on the cornea, which change.

notes.he: כלומר מפני דוקין שבעין שמשתנין גזירה למומין שבגוף אף על פי שאין משתנין:
notes.en: Due to those that change: that is, due to the dukin of the eye, which change, [there is] a decree for blemishes on the body, even though they do not change.

notes.he: דוקין שבעין דקניס מומין שבגוף דלא מישתני אטו שבעין:
notes.en: Rather, say: due to those that change: the dukin of the eye; for he penalizes [for] blemishes on the body, which do not change, on account of those in the eye.

messages.text: The mishna is also precisely formulated, as it states that Rabbi Meir says: Since it was slaughtered not according to the ruling of an expert, it is prohibited. Conclude from this wording that Rabbi Meir penalizes him for not showing it to an expert. In other words, this indicates that the animal is deemed prohibited as a penalty. It is not due to any uncertainty, as blemishes on the body do not change after death, but it is due to a rabbinic decree.
messages.quote: Since it was slaughtered not according to the ruling of an expert

notes.he: דבמומין שבגוף פליגי אבל בדוקין לא פליגי:
notes.en: The mishna is also precise: that they disagree about blemishes on the body, but about dukin they do not disagree.

notes.dh: הואיל ונשחט שלא על פי מומחה
notes.he: דלא משכח ביה ר' מאיר שום ריעותא אלא קנסו דשחטו שלא על פי מומחה ואי בדוקין שבעין הוה ליה למתני ר' מאיר אוסר הואיל ומשתנין אלא ודאי ליכא ריעותא דבמומי הגוף פליגי וקנסא קניס גזירה משום דוקין:
notes.en: Since it was slaughtered not according to an expert: for Rabbi Meir finds no flaw in it, only he penalizes him for slaughtering it not according to an expert. Had it been dukin of the eye, it should have taught: Rabbi Meir prohibits because they change. Rather, there is certainly no flaw, since they disagree about blemishes of the body, and he imposes a penalty, a decree on account of dukin.

notes.dh: מתניתין נמי דיקא דקניס ר' מאיר
notes.he: דקאמר הואיל ונשחט שלא ע"פ מומחה אסור אע"ג דהשתא הוי מום קבוע:
notes.en: The mishna is also precise that Rabbi Meir penalizes: for it says, since it was slaughtered not according to an expert, it is forbidden, even though now it is a permanent blemish.

messages.text: Conclude from it that the mishna should be understood as Rabba bar bar Ḥana explained.

A dilemma was raised before the Sages: The baraita states: Due to the blemishes on the cornea, which change. But does this mean that all blemishes on the cornea of the eye definitely change after the death of the animal? Or perhaps there are some that change after death and there are others that do not change.
messages.quote: due to the cornea, which change

notes.he: כל דוקין שבעין משתנין או דלמא בדוקין גופייהו איכא דמשתני ואיכא דלא משתני ומיהו למומין שבגוף גזרינן אטו הנך דוקין משתנין:
notes.en: That all of them change: [the question is] whether all dukin of the eye change, or perhaps among the dukin themselves there are some that change and some that do not; but in any case, for blemishes on the body we decree on account of those dukin that change.

messages.text: What is the practical difference of this dilemma?

notes.he: הא אפילו איכא דלא משתני הואיל ולא קים לן הי מישתני והי לא מישתני כולהו אסירי אם נשחטו בלא מומחה:
notes.en: What is the practical difference: for even if there are some that do not change, since we do not know which change and which do not, all are forbidden if slaughtered without an expert.

messages.text: The difference is with regard to contradicting witnesses who claim that the animal had the identical blemishes in its eye when it was alive.

notes.he: אם שחטו בלא מומחה והשתא חזינא ליה קבוע וקיימי סהדי דלא נשתנה ומראה זה היה לו מחיים:
notes.en: To contradict witnesses: if he slaughtered it without an expert, and now we see it is permanent, and witnesses stand [and testify] that it did not change and that it had this appearance while alive.

notes.he: כגון דהשתא לאחר מיתה מיתחזי מום קבוע. ואתו סהדי ואמרי דודאי כי האי גוונא חזיניה קודם שנשחט:
notes.en: To contradict witnesses: for example, now after death it appears to be a permanent blemish, and witnesses come and say: we certainly saw it like this before it was slaughtered.

messages.text: If you say that all corneas change after the death of the animal, they are liars. But if you say that there are some that change after death and there are others that do not change, the court relies on such witnesses. Therefore, what is the resolution of the dilemma?

notes.he: ואסור לדברי הכל:
notes.en: They are liars: and it is forbidden according to all.

notes.he: ושרי לר' יהודה דלא קניס:
notes.en: We rely on them: and it is permitted according to Rabbi Yehuda, who does not penalize.

notes.he: דאי אמרת דכולהו משתני הוו סהדי שקרי ואסור הבכור:
notes.en: For if you say that all of them change, the witnesses are liars, and the firstborn is forbidden.

messages.text: Come and hear, as Rabba bar bar Ḥana says:
Rabbi Yoshiya from Usha told me: Come and I will show you the corneas that change.

notes.he: אלמדך:
notes.en: Come and I will show you: [that is,] I will teach you.

messages.text: Since he said to him: Come and I will show you those that change, one can conclude by inference there are some corneas that change after death and there are others that do not change.
messages.quote: Come and I will show you the corneas that change

messages.text: § Shall we say that we learned the unattributed mishna in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, who deems a firstborn animal forbidden in all cases where it was not slaughtered based on the ruling of an expert?
messages.quote: one who is not an expert, and he examined the firstborn animal and it was slaughtered on the basis of his ruling, that animal must be buried, and the non-expert must pay compensation to the priest from his property

notes.he: דאמר לעיל אחד זה ואחד זה אסור דקתני יקבר ואע"ג דהשתא מיתחזי קבוע:
notes.en: Unattributed in accordance with Rabbi Meir: who said above, “both this and that are forbidden”; for it teaches “it must be buried,” even though now it looks permanent.

notes.he: כלומר דאע"ג דמתחזי השתא אחר שחיטה מום גמור אפילו הכי יקבר היינו כר' מאיר דקניס:
notes.en: Shall we say we learned the unattributed mishna in accordance with Rabbi Meir: that is, that even though now, after the slaughter, it appears a complete blemish, even so it must be buried; that is like Rabbi Meir, who penalizes.

messages.text: No; perhaps this is referring only to a case where there was a blemish on the cornea of the eye, which changes after the death of the animal, and everyone agrees with the ruling of the mishna in such a case.

notes.he: אמר יקבר דלדברי הכל משתנין:
notes.en: Perhaps with dukin of the eye: [there] it said “it must be buried,” since according to all they change.

notes.he: משום הכי יקבר דמשתנין:
notes.en: No, with dukin of the eye, and it is the opinion of all: that is why it must be buried, since they change.

messages.text: § The Sages taught in a baraita:
When one pays the priest for a firstborn that became forbidden, he pays one-quarter of the value of a small animal, i.e., a sheep or goat, or half of the value of a large animal, i.e., a bull.

notes.he: לכהן נותן רביע דמיו משום בכור בהמה דקה ולבכור בהמה גסה חצי דמיו. משום הכי משלם מחצה דממון המוטל בספק הוא דאיכא למימר אפסדיה כוליה דאי לא הוה שרי ליה הכי כי הוה מייתי ליה קמי מומחה גמור ושרי ליה והוה אכיל ליה והשתא בעי קבורה ואיכא למימר דלאו מידי אפסדיה דדלמא לא הוה מומא ומומחה גמור לא הוה שרי ליה ושמא לא הוה נפיל ביה לעולם מום קבוע עד שימות:
notes.en: When he pays: to the priest, he gives a quarter of its value for the firstborn of a small animal, and for the firstborn of a large animal half its value. He pays half because it is money whose ownership is in doubt. For one can say that he caused the loss of all of it: had he not permitted it this way, [the owner] would have brought it before a full expert, who would have permitted it, and [the priest] would have eaten it, and now it requires burial. And one can say that he caused no loss at all: perhaps it was not a blemish and a full expert would not have permitted it, and perhaps a permanent blemish would never have befallen it until it died.

notes.he: ואע"פ שפי' בקונטרס משום דהוי ממון המוטל בספק שמא יתירנו חכם על מום ושמא לא יתירנו לאו משום דתיתי כסומכוס אלא תקנת חכמים בעלמא הוא ואע"ג דאיירי בכל מום אפילו ידוע שיתירנו מומחה על ידו מ"מ חשיב ליה ספק קצת דשמא לא מזקיק ליה מומחה וגם לא פליג בין מום ואי הוה מיירי הך ברייתא בדוקין שבעין דוקא הוה ניחא טפי דה"נ קיימא לן כרבי יהודה כדפרישית ולדידיה אינו נקבר אלא בדוקין שבעין ועוד יש לפרש דהיינו טעמא דמשלם מחצה ששיערו חכמים דאינו שוה יותר כ"ז שעומד בספק שעדיין לא הותר ובתרומה נמי אשכחן שאינו שוה אלא כמחצה של חולין כדאמרינן בפרק אף על פי (כתובות דף נח.) כל מקום שהוזכר תרומה נותן לה כפלים בחולין ומיהו לא דמי ממש לתרומה דאסורה לזרים ואסורה בטומאה אבל בכור מומין שרי לגמרי כצבי וכאיל:
notes.en: A quarter for a small animal and half for a large one: And although Rashi explained that it is because it is money whose ownership is in doubt, [since] perhaps an expert would permit it for the blemish and perhaps he would not, this is not because it follows Sumakhos; rather, it is merely an enactment of the Sages. And even though it speaks of any blemish, even one where it is known that an expert would permit it on its account, he still considers it somewhat in doubt, for perhaps an expert would not attend to it; and also [the baraita] makes no distinction between blemishes. Had this baraita spoken specifically of dukin of the eye, it would sit better, since we hold like Rabbi Yehuda, as I explained, and according to him it is buried only for dukin of the eye. One can also explain that this is why he pays half: the Sages estimated that it is worth no more as long as it stands in doubt and has not yet been permitted. With teruma, too, we find that it is worth only about half of non-sacred produce, as we say in chapter Af Al Pi (Ketubot 58a): wherever teruma is mentioned, he gives her double in non-sacred food. But it is not truly like teruma, which is forbidden to non-priests and forbidden in impurity, whereas a blemished firstborn is entirely permitted, like a deer or a gazelle.

notes.he: ואית דאמרי משום הכי משלם מחצה ולא יותר דהוי ממון מוטל בספק הואיל ואיכא דוקין דלא משתני. למ"ה ומחצה לגבוה משום דאמרינן דמשלם דמי בשר בזול:
notes.en: He pays a quarter for a small animal. And some say: that is why he pays half and not more, since it is money whose ownership is in doubt, as there are dukin that do not change. (The text has an unclear abbreviation here; an editor’s note suggests reading: “And some say that he pays half for a large animal because we say…”, referring to Bava Batra 146b.) And half for a large one [the printed text reads “for the Most High,” apparently a slip], because we say that he pays the value of the meat at a cheap price.

messages.text: What is the reason for this discrepancy?
messages.quote: one-quarter of the value of a small animal, or half of the value of a large animal

notes.he: רביע לדקה ומחצה לגסה:
notes.en: What is the reason: [for] a quarter for a small animal and half for a large one?

notes.he: להאי מחצה:
notes.en: What is the reason: for this half.

messages.text: The loss of this bull is a relatively great loss, and the loss of that sheep or goat is a small loss.

notes.he: לפיכך תשלומין מרובין:
notes.en: A large animal, its loss is great: therefore the payment is great.

notes.he: דזה בהמה גסה מפסידו הרבה הילכך משלם הרבה מחצה:
notes.en: For this one, a large animal, he causes it great loss; therefore he pays much: half.

notes.he: בהמה דקה דהפסדה מועט דאינה גדולה כ"כ משלם רביע:
notes.en: And this one: a small animal, whose loss is small since it is not so big, he pays a quarter.

messages.text: If so, let him pay in accordance with the actual loss incurred. In other words, if he paid the same proportion of the value of a sheep or goat, he would still be paying less than half the value of a bull.
messages.quote: that sheep or goat is a small loss

notes.he: לזה חצי דמיו המרובין ולזה חצי דמיו המעוטין:
notes.en: Let him pay according to the loss: to this one half of its larger value, and to that one half of its smaller value.

notes.dh: אי הפסדה מועט לשלם לפום פסידה
notes.he: כלומר מחצה מההוא מועט ומאי שנא רביע:
notes.en: If its loss is small, let him pay according to its loss: that is, half of that small [value]. Why is it different, [that he pays] a quarter?

messages.text: The Sages touched upon it and determined that he should pay only one-quarter, due to the decree against those who raise small livestock in Eretz Yisrael, as these animals cause damage to the land. As a result, such animals may be raised only in specific areas, which means the priest was spared exertion, and therefore the Sages required one to pay only one-quarter of the value.
messages.lead: Rav Huna bar Manoaḥ says in the name of Rav Aḥa bar Ika:

notes.dh: משום גזירת מגדלי בהמה דקה נגעו בה
notes.he: משום טורח מגדלי בהמה דקה שיש בה טורח גדול לגדלה וזה שהתיר הבכור הצילו לכהן מטורח גדול דשמא אם הראהו לאחר לא היה מתירו לו והיה לו עוד טיפול מרובה עד שיפול בו מום להכי נגעו בו דלא משלם אלא רביע. ל"א מפני גזירת מגדלי בהמה דקה שעוברין על דברי חכמים כדתנן (ב"ק דף עט:) אין מגדלין בהמה דקה בא"י קנסוהו חכמים דלא לישקל אלא ריבעא. ולא מפי המורה:
notes.en: They touched upon it due to the decree on those who raise small livestock: due to the trouble of those who raise small livestock, for raising it is a great trouble; and this one who permitted the firstborn saved the priest from great trouble, for perhaps had [the owner] shown it to another, he would not have permitted it, and he would have had much more care [of it] until a blemish befell it. Therefore they touched upon it, so that he pays only a quarter. Another version: due to the decree on those who raise small livestock, who transgress the words of the Sages, as we learned (Bava Kamma 79b): one may not raise small livestock in the Land of Israel; the Sages penalized him so that he takes only a quarter. (Rashi adds: and not from the teacher’s mouth, [i.e., he did not receive this second version from his teacher].)

notes.he: פירוש שהחמירו עליהם חכמים שלא לגדלם כי אם בחורשין חוץ ליישוב ויש בה טורח גדול ואינו שוה אלא רביע דהיינו מחצה פחות מן הגסה וגם בקונטרס פירש כן מפני טורח גזרו לה אבל לא דקדק ליישב לשון גזירה:
notes.en: Due to the decree on those who raise small livestock: that is, the Sages were strict with them not to raise them except in woodlands outside settled areas, and this involves great trouble, and it is worth only a quarter, which is half as much as the large animal. Rashi too explained that they decreed it because of the trouble, but he did not take care to account for the word “decree.”

notes.dh: לא משום קנס מגדלי בהמה דקה
notes.he: דאסור לגדל בהמה דקה בא"י:
notes.en: Due to the penalty on those who raise small livestock: for it is forbidden to raise small livestock in the Land of Israel. [Rabbeinu Gershom’s heading reads “penalty” where our text reads “decree.”]

notes.he: ועסקינן דהאי בכור של בהמת כהן הוא והוא גידל הבהמה דקה:
notes.en: And we are dealing with a case where this firstborn is from a priest’s animal, and he raised the small livestock.

messages.text: Mishna

If a judge issued a judgment and erred, so that he exempted a liable party or found an innocent party liable, or if he ruled that a pure item is impure or ruled that an impure item is pure, and by doing so he caused a litigant a monetary loss, then what he did is done, i.e., the judgment stands, and the judge must pay damages from his home, i.e., from his personal funds.

notes.he: בפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף ו.) פריך מינה לר' אבהו שאמר שנים שדנו אין דיניהן דין ותימה מנא ליה דמיירי ביחיד אי משום דקתני דן את הדין לשון יחיד הא בריש אלו טריפות (חולין דף מד:) קתני דן את הדין ולא מיירי ביחיד כדקתני וכולן רשאין ליקח ויש לומר דהתם קתני דומיא דעדים אבל מתני' דהכא מיירי כולה ביחיד דקתני סיפא ואם היה מומחה לבית דין כו' ומעשה בר' טרפון כו' ורישא נמי מי שאינו מומחה וראה את הבכור:
notes.en: He judged the case…: In the first chapter of Sanhedrin (6a) it raises an objection from this against Rabbi Abbahu, who said: two who judged, their judgment is no judgment. And it is puzzling: from where does it know that this speaks of a single judge? If because it teaches “he judged the case” in the singular, at the beginning of Elu Tereifot (Ḥullin 44b) it teaches “he judged the case” and does not speak of a single [judge], as it teaches, “and all of them may buy.” One can say that there it is taught in parallel with witnesses, but the mishna here speaks entirely of a single [judge], as the latter clause teaches, “And if he was an expert for the court…,” and “an incident with Rabbi Tarfon…,” and the first clause too: “one who is not an expert and examined the firstborn.”

messages.text: And if the judge was an expert for the court, he is exempt from liability to pay.

notes.dh: מתני' ואם היה מומחה לב"ד פטור
notes.he: דלא מצי מימר ליה אמאי דיינת ליה הואיל ולא בקי בדיני:
notes.en: Mishna. And if he was an expert for the court, he is exempt: for [the litigant] cannot say to him: Why did you judge me, since you are not versed in the laws?

notes.he: לרבים דלא טעה אלא בשקול הדעת פטור מלשלם:
notes.en: And if he was an expert: for the public, who erred only in deliberation, he is exempt from paying.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches that a judge who errs must pay compensation for the damage he caused. Shall we say that we learned the unattributed mishna in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, who rules that there is liability for damage caused by indirect action?
messages.quote: the judge must pay damages from his home

notes.he: בב"ק בפרק הגוזל עצים (בבא קמא דף ק.) מחיצת הכרם שנפרצה אומר לו גדור נתייאש הימנה ולא גדרה הרי זה קידש וחייב באחריותו. גרמי דגרם לאסור תבואתו של חבירו:
notes.en: Gemara. Rabbi Meir, who judges [liability for] indirect damage: in Bava Kamma, chapter HaGozel Etzim (Bava Kamma 100a): a vineyard’s partition that was breached, [and the owner of the field] says to him: Fence it; he gave up on it and did not fence it: he has rendered [the grain] forbidden and is liable for it. Indirect damage, for he caused his fellow’s grain to become forbidden.

notes.dh: לימא תנן סתמא כרבי מאיר כו'
notes.he: תימה דלא דייק הכא מרישא דמי שאינו מומחה ורואה את הבכור ונשחט על פיו הרי זה יקבר וישלם מביתו דההיא מה נפשך כרבי מאיר אתיא דדאין דינא דגרמי דלא מתוקמא בנשא ונתן ביד דהא נשחט על פיו קתני ובהגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף ק.) לא משכח התם משנה דדאין ר"מ דינא דגרמי אלא מברייתא דמחיצת הכרם והוה ליה לאיתויי מהך ובהגוזל בתרא (שם דף קיז:) גבי ההוא דאחויי אחוי דסבר למיחייביה ממתניתין דדן את הדין וקדחי אמאי לא חייביה מהך:
notes.en: Shall we say we learned the unattributed mishna in accordance with Rabbi Meir…: It is puzzling that it does not infer here from the first clause, “one who is not an expert and examined the firstborn and it was slaughtered on his ruling, it must be buried and he pays from his house.” That, whichever way you look at it, follows Rabbi Meir, who judges indirect damage, since it cannot be explained as [where] he took and gave with his hand, as it teaches “it was slaughtered on his ruling.” And in HaGozel Kamma (Bava Kamma 100a) it finds no mishna where Rabbi Meir judges indirect damage, only the baraita of the vineyard’s partition; it should have cited this one. And in HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 117b), concerning that man who pointed out [another’s property], where he wanted to hold him liable from the mishna “he judged the case” and it was rejected, why did he not hold him liable from this one?

notes.he: בב"ק בפרק הגוזל עצים. והאי גורם בדבורו לאבד ממון:
notes.en: Who judges indirect damage: in Bava Kamma, chapter HaGozel Etzim. And this one causes the loss of money by his speech.

messages.text: This is referring to a case where a judge took the item in question from one litigant and gave it to the other litigant with his hand, and therefore he directly caused the damage.

notes.he: שנטל בידים מזה ונתן לזה. ולא גורם הוא אלא גוזל:
notes.en: Where he took and gave with his hand: he took with his own hands from this one and gave to that one; he is not [merely] a cause but a robber.

messages.text: Granted, the case where he finds an innocent party liable is in a case where the judge took the item in question from the innocent party and gave it to the other litigant with his hand.
messages.quote: took the item in question from one litigant and gave it to the other litigant with his hand

notes.dh: בשלמא חייב את הזכאי משכחת נשא ונתן ביד
notes.he: שנטל הוא המעות ממנו בידו ופרעו לבעל דין:
notes.en: Granted, he found an innocent party liable, one finds it where he took and gave with his hand: he himself took the money from him with his hand and paid the litigant.

messages.text: But what are the circumstances of his giving the item from one to another with regard to the clause of: He exempts a liable party? It is if the judge said to the litigant only: You are exempt from liability to pay, but the judge did not take the item in question from one litigant and give it to the other litigant with his hand.

notes.dh: אלא זיכה את החייב היכי דמי
notes.he: בעל כרחך לא משכחת לה דעביד מידי אלא פטור אתה קאמר ליה:
notes.en: But he exempted a liable party, what are the circumstances: perforce you cannot find that he did anything; he only said to him: You are exempt.

messages.text: It is referring to a case where the lender had collateral from the borrower, and the judge took it from him and gave it back to the other party.

notes.he: למלוה וזה פטר את הלוה ונטל את המשכון מיד המלוה והחזירו ללוה:
notes.en: That he had collateral: [that is,] the lender; and this [judge] exempted the borrower and took the collateral from the lender’s hand and returned it to the borrower.

notes.he: כגון שהיה לנתבע משכון בידו של תובע ונטלו הימנו ונתנו לזה:
notes.en: For example, where the defendant’s collateral was in the plaintiff’s hand, and he took it from him and gave it to this one.

messages.text: In the case of: He ruled that a pure item is impure, how could he cause a loss with his own hands? It is where he had the litigant’s ritually pure item touch a creeping animal to emphasize that he believes it was already impure, and he thereby imparted impurity to it.

notes.he: הביאו טהרות לפניו לישאל עליהן ואמר טמאות הן ונטל שרץ אחד ונגע בהן כדי שלא יהא עוד ספק בהן ויעמיד דבריו:
notes.en: That he had a creeping animal touch them: they brought foodstuffs before him to ask about them, and he said they are impure, and he took a creeping animal and touched them with it, so that there would be no more doubt about them, and to uphold his words.

notes.he: בידים:
notes.en: That he had a creeping animal touch them: with his hands.

messages.text: In the case of: He ruled that an impure item is pure, how could he cause a loss with his own hands? It is where he mixed this impure produce of the litigant’s with the litigant’s ritually pure produce, and he thereby caused all of the produce to be considered impure. When an expert judge later rules that that produce is actually impure, the result is that the entire mixture contains impure produce, and the judge caused this damage directly.

notes.he: שהביא טהרות לפניו לישאל עליהן ואמר טהורות ונטלן הוא עצמו ועירבן עם פירותיו של נשאל לסוף אמר חכם מומחה טמאות הן וטימאו את השאר שנתערבו בהן:
notes.en: That he mixed them with his produce: [the questioner] brought foodstuffs before him to ask about them, and he said they are pure, and he himself took them and mixed them with the produce of the one who asked. In the end an expert sage said they are impure, and they made impure the rest with which they were mixed.

notes.he: כגון שנטל פירות טמאין ואמר טהורין הן ועירבן בפירות חברו דקא עבד בידים דהפסיד פירותיו:
notes.en: He declared the impure pure: for example, he took impure produce and said they are pure, and mixed them with his fellow’s produce; he acted with his hands and caused the loss of his produce.

messages.text: Mishna

Apropos the previous mishna, which taught that a judge who was an expert for the court and who erred is exempt from payment, this mishna teaches: There was an incident involving a cow whose womb was removed, and when Rabbi Tarfon was consulted he ruled that it is an animal with a wound that will cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa], which is forbidden for consumption. And based on the ruling of Rabbi Tarfon, the questioner fed it to the dogs.

notes.he: רחם שלה:
notes.en: Mishna. Its em: its womb.

notes.he: ששאלו לו עליה אם טריפה היא והאכילה לכלבים:
notes.en: And Rabbi Tarfon fed it to the dogs: for they asked him about it, whether it is a tereifa, and he fed it to the dogs.

notes.he: בית ולד שלה:
notes.en: Its em: its birth chamber.

notes.he: דאמר דטרפה היא:
notes.en: And fed it to the dogs: for he said that it is a tereifa.

messages.text: And the incident came before the Sages of the court in Yavne, and they ruled that such an animal is permitted and is not a tereifa.

A cow or pig does not emerge from Alexandria of Egypt unless the residents sever its womb so that it will not give birth in the future. The breeds of cows and pigs in Alexandria were of exceptional quality and the people of Alexandria did not want them reproduced elsewhere. The fact that these animals lived long lives after their wombs were removed proves that the hysterectomy did not render them tereifot.

notes.he: מפני שפרות וחזירות שלהן מעולין מאד ומוכרין אותן ביוקר ורוצין שלא ילדו במלכות אחרת כדי שיהו צריכין להם וחותכין האם שלה ואינה מתה הילכך לאו טריפה היא:
notes.en: So that it will not give birth: because their cows and sows are very superior and they sell them dearly, and they want them not to give birth in another kingdom, so that [others] will need them. They cut out its womb and it does not die; therefore it is not a tereifa.

messages.text: Your donkey is gone, Tarfon, as he believed he was required to compensate the owner for the cow that he ruled to be a tereifa.

notes.he: הפסדת חמור שתשלמנו לבעל הפרה:
notes.en: Your donkey is gone, Tarfon: you have lost a donkey, which you will pay to the owner of the cow.

notes.he: כלומר הפסדת חמורך. כלומר שתפרע לו חמורך תחת פרתו שהפסדתו:
notes.en: Your donkey is gone, Tarfon: that is, you have lost your donkey; that is, you will pay him your donkey in place of his cow that you caused him to lose.

messages.text: @Rabbi Tarfon you are an expert for the court, and any expert for the court is exempt from liability to pay.
Gemara

But let Rabbi Akiva derive his ruling from the fact that Rabbi Tarfon erred concerning a matter that appears in the Mishna, as the ruling permitting an animal whose womb has been removed is recorded in a mishna (see Ḥullin 54a), and with regard to anyone who erred concerning a matter that appears in the Mishna, the decision is revoked, as this is considered an obvious mistake.
messages.quote: any expert for the court is exempt from liability to pay

notes.he: דאי נמי לאו מומחה הוא פטור דטועה בדבר משנה הוא דתנן באלו טריפות (חולין דף נד.) ניטלה האם כשירה וטעה בדבר משנה חוזר בדיבורו בסנהדרין (דף לג.) וכיון דאי קיימא פרה הוה מצי למיהדר ביה ולמשרייה אישתכח דמה שאמר לאו כלום הוא זה וזה שהאכילה לכלבים איהו הוא דאפסיד אנפשיה:
notes.en: Gemara. And let him derive it: that even if he were not an expert he would be exempt, since he erred in a matter [stated in a] mishna, as we learned in Elu Tereifot (Ḥullin 54a): if the womb was removed, it is kosher; and one who errs in a matter [stated in a] mishna retracts, in Sanhedrin (33a). And since, had the cow still existed, he could have retracted and permitted it, it turns out that what he said is nothing, and this one who fed it to the dogs caused the loss to himself.

notes.he: דפטור מלשלם משום דטועה בדבר משנה חוזר דתנן ניטלה האם שלה כשרה:
notes.en: And let him derive: that he is exempt from paying, because one who errs in a matter [stated in a] mishna retracts, for we learned: if its womb was removed, it is kosher.

messages.text: In other words, Rabbi Tarfon’s decision was not binding, and therefore when the owner fed the cow to the dogs, he acted on the basis of a ruling with no validity and thereby caused his own loss.

Rabbi Akiva states one reason and adds another reason. One reason is that in the case of one who errs in a matter that appears in the Mishna, the decision is revoked. Another reason is that even if you erred in a deliberation, you are a judge accepted as an expert for the public, and any judge accepted as an expert for the public is exempt from liability to pay.

notes.he: דאפילו הוה קיימא לא מצי למיהדר ביה ולמישרייה ואישתכח דאיסורו איסור ואתה הפסדתו אפילו הכי פטור אתה מלשלם דמומחה אתה. שיקול הדעת מפרש בפרק קמא דסנהדרין (דף ו.) כגון תרי תנאי או תרי אמוראי דפליגי ולא איתמר הילכתא לא כמר ולא כמר וסוגייא דעלמא כחד מינייהו ואזיל האי ועבד כאידך מה שעשה עשוי ומשלם מביתו:
notes.en: Alternatively, you erred in deliberation: where even if it still existed you could not retract and permit it, so your prohibition stands as a prohibition and you caused the loss; even so you are exempt from paying, since you are an expert. Deliberation is explained in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (6a): for example, two Tannaim or two Amoraim who disagree, and the halakha was not stated like either, and the general practice follows one of them, and this one went and acted like the other: what he did is done, and he pays from his house.

messages.text: Mishna

In the case of an individual who takes payment to be one who examines firstborn animals to determine whether they are blemished, one may not slaughter the firstborn on the basis of his ruling, unless he was an expert …

notes.he: דלמא משום אגרא קשרי ליה:
notes.en: Mishna. One may not slaughter: lest he permit it for the sake of the fee.

notes.he: דאיכא למימר בשביל שכר שנוטל מתירו:
notes.en: One may not slaughter on his ruling: for one could say that he permits it because of the fee he takes.

messages.text: The mishna continues on 29a: an expert like Ila in Yavne, whom the Sages permitted to take a fee for examining a firstborn, whether it turned out unblemished or blemished.
